newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Daewoo seen dominating E.Europe car sales.
newsitem.headline: Daewoo seen dominating E.Europe car sales.

text.p: South Korean conglomerate Daewoo Group, which sold only a handful of cars in former communist Europe until 1995, is now poised to dominate the region's auto industry, according to a new study.
"Daewoo is obviously taking over," said Elaine Hardy, director of the study by British auto consultants Harbour Wade Brown.
"They're really going places, and the automakers from Japan and western Europe are losing out," Hardy told Reuters.

Daewoo has announced a staggering number of investments in the region over the past two years with plans to spend billions of dollars to build vehicles and parts in the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Russia, Slovakia and Ukraine. It also has said it would consider projects in Bulgaria and Croatia.
"Their objectives are to build over one million light vehicles a year in the region by 2001," Hardy said.
"The question is whether they plan to use their production capacity to satisfy demand in eastern Europe or to export to western Europe. I suspect it's both, and it is a bit worrying."

While Daewoo's purchase of state-owned automakers in the region has grabbed the biggest headlines, its real gain from the acquisitions in the long term might be a vast networks of sales and service outlets.

"We estimate that Daewoo now has 621 dealers in the region -- second only to AvtoVAZ, which has 828 dealers," Hardy said, referring to Russia's largest automaker. AvtoVAZ makes Lada and Samara cars and Niva off-road vehicles.
"It's important to build an effective dealer network to be near customers, and Daewoo is there on the forecourt for people to visit showrooms and buy cars," she added.

Daewoo's distribution network enabled it to rank fourth in regional sales in 1996 with 165,000 units, behind AvtoVAZ with 585,000 units, Volkswagen AG with 213,000 units and Fiat SPA with 199,000 units, according to data derived from the study.
